name: voice-scribe
description: High-quality real-time voice-to-text for VS Code with live rewriting — ElevenLabs Scribe v2 or Google Cloud Speech-to-Text V2

commands.title: Voice Scribe: Polish Last Paragraph with Claude Code
Voice Scribe: Generate Keyterms from Open Files (Claude Opus)
Voice Scribe: Select Google Model (latency vs. accuracy)

enumDescriptions: ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime (requires an API key)
Google Cloud Speech-to-Text V2 streaming (uses gcloud Application Default Credentials; no API key). Model is chosen with 'voiceScribe.googleModel'.
voiceScribe.provider.description: Speech-to-text provider. Switch with the 'Voice Scribe: Select Provider' command. ElevenLabs uses an API key; Google uses gcloud ADC (run 'gcloud auth application-default login').

voiceScribe.apiKey.description: Your ElevenLabs API key for speech-to-text. Only used when the provider is 'elevenlabs'.

voiceScribe.googleProject.description: Google Cloud project ID for the Google provider. Leave empty to auto-detect from your gcloud Application Default Credentials.

voiceScribe.googleLocation.description: Google Cloud region for Chirp streaming (e.g. 'eu', 'us', 'europe-west4', 'us-central1'). The client uses the matching regional endpoint and recognizer location; the region must support the chosen model.

enumDescriptions: Long (default, recommended) — near-instant: first text ~0.8s, updates every ~60ms. Best for dictation. Requires an explicit language (no auto-detect).
Short — same low latency as 'long', tuned for brief utterances. Requires an explicit language.
Chirp 3 — best multilingual accuracy and code-switching, and the only option supporting language auto-detect. Streams in ~5-second blocks, so text appears ~5s behind speech.
Chirp 2 — previous multilingual generation, same ~5-second streaming behaviour. Not available in the 'eu' location; use e.g. 'europe-west4' or 'us-central1'.
voiceScribe.googleModel.markdownDescription:
Google Speech-to-Text V2 model used for streaming transcription.

**Latency vs. accuracy** (measured, `eu` region): `long` returns first text in ~0.8s and updates every ~60ms; `chirp_3` emits only once per ~5 seconds of audio. On English the two produce identical transcripts, so `long` is the better default. For Czech and other non-English speech `chirp_3` is noticeably more accurate — switch if accuracy matters more than responsiveness.

Only the Chirp models support `voiceScribe.language: auto`; with `long`/`short` you must pick a language.

enumDescriptions: Auto-detect (let the API detect the spoken language)
voiceScribe.language.description: Language you are speaking in for transcription (ISO 639-1 code). Set to 'auto' to let the API detect your language automatically.

enumDescriptions: Always wrap committed text in a line comment
Auto-comment in code files, plain text in prose files (markdown, plaintext, etc.)
voiceScribe.insertMode.description: How committed transcriptions are inserted into the editor.

voiceScribe.removeFiller.description: Remove filler words (um, uh, like, you know, etc.) from transcriptions.

voiceScribe.enableVoiceCommands.description: Enable voice commands (undo, redo, delete line, save, stop, etc.). When enabled, spoken commands are executed instead of inserted as text.

enumDescriptions: Insert committed text into the active text editor (default)
Send committed text to the integrated terminal
Noisy environment (open office, cafe). Rejects more non-speech.
Quiet room or headset. More sensitive to speech.
voiceScribe.vadSensitivity.description: Voice Activity Detection sensitivity preset. Controls how aggressively non-speech audio is rejected.

word.description: The word or phrase to boost recognition for

boost.description: Boost factor (1.0-10.0). Higher values increase recognition likelihood.

voiceScribe.customVocabulary.description: Custom vocabulary for improved recognition of domain-specific terms. Max 200 entries. Each entry requires a 'word' and optionally 'boost' (1.0-10.0) and 'phonemes'.

voiceScribe.audioChunkMs.description: Size of each audio chunk sent to the speech API, in milliseconds. Smaller chunks reach the recognizer sooner (lower latency) at the cost of slightly more network messages. 20ms matches the ~60ms cadence at which the low-latency models emit results; raise it if you see network overhead.

voiceScribe.audioDevice.description: Optional: explicit input device name. On Windows, use the DirectShow device name (run `ffmpeg -list_devices true -f dshow -i dummy` to list). Leave empty to auto-detect the first available input device. Has no effect on macOS/Linux (system default is used).

voiceScribe.recordingPrefix.description: Custom string inserted at the cursor when recording starts (e.g. '// '). Set via the 'Voice Scribe: Set Recording Prefix' command.

voiceScribe.autoVocabulary.description: Automatically extract identifiers from open files and boost them in the speech recognition vocabulary.

enumDescriptions: Haiku — fastest, cheapest, great for paragraph polish (default)
Sonnet — balanced quality/speed, better with complex technical prose
voiceScribe.polishModel.description: Claude Code model used by the polish feature. Invoked via `claude -p --model <alias>`.

voiceScribe.polishTimeoutMs.description: Maximum time (milliseconds) to wait for Claude Code to return a polished paragraph before aborting.

voiceScribe.polishOnPauseMs.description: If greater than 0, automatically polish the last paragraph after this many milliseconds of silence during recording. Set to 0 to disable (default). Recommended: 4000-8000.

voiceScribe.keyterms.description: Keyterms biased during transcription (Scribe v2 Realtime). Max 50 entries, each ≤20 chars. Adds ~20% to per-minute cost when non-empty. Use 'Voice Scribe: Generate Keyterms from Open Files (Claude Opus)' to auto-fill from README.md, CLAUDE.md, and currently open files.
